name: Immersive web
summary: Public pages built around one real-time 3D scene the visitor can drive: product viewers and configurators, a 3D hero for a company site, a spatial subject taught in the browser - with three.js, React Three Fiber or model-viewer.
summaryVi: Trang công khai dựng quanh một cảnh 3D thời gian thực mà khách tự điều khiển: xem và cấu hình sản phẩm, hero 3D cho trang doanh nghiệp, môn học có tính không gian - bằng three.js, React Three Fiber hoặc model-viewer.
optimisesFor: The moment a stranger turns the object themselves - on a page that had already told them what it is before the scene arrived.

skill.name: immersive-web-design
skill.description: Design, build, restyle or review public web pages built around a real-time 3D scene - three.js, WebGL, WebGPU, React Three Fiber, model-viewer or Spline. Use it whenever a page gets a 3D product viewer or configurator, a 3D hero, a scroll-driven scene, a rotating model, an exploded view or a glTF/GLB embed; when asked to make a site more immersive, interactive or 'like those award-winning 3D sites'; when deciding whether something should be real-time 3D, a video or an image at all; when a canvas is slow, hot, janky on a phone, blank on iOS, heavy to load or hurting LCP; when wiring poster images, lazy loading, pixel-ratio caps, Draco or KTX2 compression, context loss or disposal; or when a 3D page needs a keyboard path, reduced-motion behaviour or a fallback. Covers product review and showcase pages, company and studio sites, and course pages for spatial subjects. Not for games, full-screen 3D applications and editors, ordinary marketing pages with no scene, or admin tools.
skill.descriptionVi: Thiết kế, dựng, chỉnh lại hoặc review trang web công khai có cảnh 3D thời gian thực - three.js, WebGL, WebGPU, React Three Fiber, model-viewer.

when: a product page where the visitor rotates, opens or configures the product in 3D
a company, studio or portfolio site whose hero is an interactive scene
a course or explainer page for a subject that is spatial - anatomy, mechanics, architecture, geography
a request for three.js, WebGL, WebGPU, React Three Fiber, model-viewer, a GLB embed or a scroll-driven 3D section
a question about whether something should be real-time 3D, a pre-rendered video or a still
a 3D page that is slow, hot, blank on a phone, or failing an accessibility or performance review
notFor: a marketing or landing page with no real-time scene - use the consumer-web pack, whose JavaScript budget this pack spends several times over
games and full-screen 3D applications - editors, CAD viewers, anatomy atlases a user works in for an hour; there the viewport is the product and the page-first rule here is wrong
internal tools, admin panels and dashboards - use the erp pack; a scene is decoration to an operator on their two-hundredth visit
installed mobile apps - use the mobile-app pack
a fixed camera fly-through nobody can steer - that is a video, and it should be shipped as one
charts and data visualisation, including 3D charts - core's chart rules cover them and a perspective axis breaks them

surfaces.chrome: minimal - a header floating over the stage, on an opaque plate once anything scrolls beneath it
surfaces.canvas: the stage: a near-black surface the scene is lit against, with a light page surface for long-form sections
surfaces.content: HTML in its own lane beside the scene, or on an opaque plate over it - never set directly on a moving render
surfaces.floating: plates, the option picker and hotspot popovers - one luminance step above the stage, no shadow
surfaces.accent: one blue with a value per surface, reserved for the primary action and the selected option
surfaces.semantic: success/warning/danger, in forms and scene status only

platform.note: Touch first, and touch is where a scene does the most damage: a canvas that takes every gesture is a hole in the page a thumb cannot scroll across. Vertical movement always belongs to the page.

density: low - 16px base, one scene per page, and at most one idea on the stage at a time

references.title: The scene - whether to build it, and how to stage it
Budget - bytes, frames, loading and the device
Access - keyboard, touch, reduced motion and failure

assets.note: the scene frame, its four states, the stage layout and the plate
the reference mount in plain three.js - lazy import, capped pixel ratio, render on demand, context loss, disposal
